input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Run comparison view with diff mode in the Dashboard

## Description

This epic delivers a run comparison capability in the Dashboard: users can
select two or more training or pipeline runs and view their parameters and
metrics side by side, including a diff presentation that highlights which
parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. This replaces the
current workflow in which comparison happens in exported spreadsheets because
parameters and metrics are only visible on per-run pages.

## Scope

- Multi-select of two or more runs from the runs list in the Dashboard.
- A comparison view presenting the selected runs' parameters and metrics side
  by side.
- A diff mode over the same comparison surface that highlights which parameters
  and metrics differ between two selected runs.
- Comparison works within a single project only (cross-cluster and
  cross-project comparison are out of scope per the strategy).
- Validation that the comparison view works for Data Science Pipelines runs as
  well as training runs, using the run metadata already surfaced to the
  Dashboard (Data Science Pipelines is a passive component in this strategy —
  no pipeline-side code changes).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a runs list in the Dashboard, when the user selects two or more runs,
  then a comparison view opens showing each selected run's parameters and
  metrics side by side.
- Given two runs selected for comparison, when the user activates the diff
  view, then the parameters and metrics that changed between the two runs are
  highlighted, and unchanged values remain visible for context.
- Given runs of both kinds (training runs and Data Science Pipelines runs) in
  the same project, when they are selected together, then their parameters and
  metrics are displayed in the comparison view.
- Given runs from different projects, when the user attempts a comparison,
  then the selection is limited to a single project (no cross-project
  comparison).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters
  and metrics side by side in the Dashboard.
- **HLR-3 (P1)**: Run "diff" view highlighting which parameters and metrics
  changed between two selected runs — a presentation mode of the same
  comparison surface as HLR-1, consolidated into this epic rather than split
  out (same component and team; splitting would build the same surface twice).

# Link registered model versions to producing runs

## Description

This epic delivers run lineage in the Model Registry: a registered model
version records a reference to the run (training or pipeline run) that produced
it, so that downstream consumers — including the Dashboard's comparison
capability — can resolve which run created a given model version. The registry
already serves as the source of truth for training lineage; this epic extends
that lineage to the run level.

## Scope

- Recording, on registered model versions, a reference to the run that
  produced them, using the Model Registry's existing extension point for
  structured metadata on model versions (the mechanism is an implementation
  decision for the Model Registry team).
- Exposing the run reference through the Model Registry's existing REST
  interface so that clients can retrieve the producing run for a model
  version.
- Support for both training-run and pipeline-run references.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a model version registered after this change, when it is created from
  a run, then the version carries a reference to that producing run that is
  retrievable via the Model Registry REST API.
- Given a model version with a run reference, when the reference is resolved,
  then it identifies the run within the same project (single-project scope per
  the strategy's out-of-scope list).
- Given model versions registered before this change, when queried, then they
  remain readable with no regression (absence of a run reference on legacy
  versions is handled gracefully).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P1)**: Registered model versions link back to the run that produced
  them (registry-side linkage; the Dashboard-facing entry point that opens a
  comparison from the registry is delivered separately by the Dashboard team).

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry view

## Description

This epic delivers the Model Registry entry point for run comparison: from a
registered model version in the Dashboard's registry view, users can open the
run comparison capability populated with the run that produced that version,
without navigating back to the runs list. The Dashboard owns the registry UI,
so this epic is owned by the Dashboard team and builds on two prerequisites:
the run comparison view (its navigation target) and the run linkage recorded on
registered model versions (its data source).

## Scope

- An action on a registered model version in the Dashboard's Model Registry
  view that opens the run comparison view populated with the producing run.
- Graceful handling of model versions that carry no run reference (legacy
  versions registered before linkage existed).
- Single-project scope: the opened comparison stays within the model version's
  project.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version that carries a producing-run reference,
  when the user activates the compare action in the registry view, then the
  run comparison view opens with the producing run pre-selected.
- Given a registered model version with no run reference, when the registry
  view is displayed, then the compare affordance is absent or disabled without
  errors.
- Given the compare action is used, when the comparison view opens, then the
  user can add further runs from the same project to the comparison.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P1)**: "so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry" —
  the Dashboard-facing half of HLR-2, delivered by the Dashboard team which
  owns the registry UI.

# Document the run comparison workflow

## Description

This epic delivers Red Hat documentation for the run comparison capability:
user-facing topics covering how to compare training and pipeline runs from
both entry points — the runs list and the Model Registry — including the diff
view and the model-version-to-run linkage. Documentation is authored after the
implementation epics complete so it describes what was actually built.

## Scope

Content outline (new documentation topics):

- Comparing runs from the runs list: selecting two or more runs and reading
  the side-by-side parameters and metrics view.
- Using the diff view to see which parameters and metrics changed between two
  runs.
- Opening a comparison from the Model Registry: how registered model versions
  link to their producing run and how to launch a comparison from a model
  version.
- What is and is not supported: single-project comparisons; no automatic
  best-run selection or promotion; no cross-cluster or cross-project
  comparison.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation topics cover the comparison workflow starting from the runs
  list, including multi-select, the side-by-side view, and the diff view.
- Documentation topics cover the comparison workflow starting from the Model
  Registry, including the model-version run linkage and the compare action.
- All documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented
  capability (reviewed by engineering for accuracy against the shipped
  behavior) before publication.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)**: Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the
  runs list and the registry.
